data.title: Weak Transport Layer Security Configuration
data.summary: Services supported obsolete protocol versions and weak cipher suites, or presented certificates that do not validate, weakening the confidentiality and integrity guarantees that TLS is deployed to provide.
data.description:
TLS protects data in transit only to the extent that both ends agree on strong parameters. Support for SSLv3, TLS 1.0 and 1.1 keeps known-broken constructions available, and weak cipher suites — RC4, 3DES, anything without forward secrecy, export-grade — remain negotiable where they are enabled.

Certificate problems are the more frequent operational issue: expired certificates, names that do not match, and self-signed certificates on internal services. Their real harm is cumulative — users are trained to click through warnings, and once that habit exists, an attacker's certificate is accepted too.

Missing HSTS leaves a downgrade window on the first connection, which is where interception is easiest.
data.recommendation:
* Permit only TLS 1.2 and 1.3, with forward-secret cipher suites; disable everything earlier.
* Use certificates from a trusted authority, including internally, and automate renewal.
* Deploy HSTS with a long max-age on public services.
* Monitor expiry and configuration continuously rather than at audit time.
data.short_recommendation: Allow only TLS 1.2 and 1.3 with modern cipher suites.
